title: Incident #104: Misconfigured Supervision Strategy Leaving Stale Downstream Workers
solutionExplanation: Fixed Incident #104 by reconfiguring supervisor with strategy => rest_for_one, intensity => 5, period => 10, and setting all pipeline workers to permanent restart.

otpDocCards.description: Returns a list of all current children managed by the supervisor, including their PIDs and statuses.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why is rest_for_one mandatory for [db -> cache -> http] pipelines instead of one_for_one?

options.label: Because when an upstream worker (like cache) restarts, downstream workers (like http) must be restarted to invalidate stale handles and reconnect to the new PID.
options.explanation: rest_for_one guarantees that any child dependent on an upstream worker is cleanly restarted in sequence.

options.label: Because one_for_one only allows two children total.
options.explanation: one_for_one allows any number of children, but restarts them in total isolation.

options.label: Because rest_for_one executes 10x faster than one_for_one.
options.explanation: Restart strategy choice is about architectural dependency correctness, not raw execution speed.

options.label: Because the Erlang compiler rejects one_for_one on pipelines.
options.explanation: The compiler cannot know your architectural dependencies; you must choose the correct strategy.

incidentAlert.symptom: When auth_cache crashes under memory pressure, it never restarts (leaving the cache dead), and downstream api_router continues running with broken references!
incidentAlert.rootCauseHint: init/1 in incident_wrong_strategy.erl configured strategy => one_for_one instead of rest_for_one, set intensity => 0 (so the very first crash kills the supervisor!), and marked auth_cache as restart => temporary.
incidentAlert.fixObjective: Fix init([]) to return strategy => rest_for_one, intensity => 5, period => 10, and ensure all 3 pipeline children ([worker_db, worker_cache, worker_http]) have restart => permanent and type => worker.
incidentAlert.impact: Total failure of authentication routing when cache worker crashes.
